gehaeuse_oeffnen.werkzeug: 3/32 inch bzw. 2.3 mm Innensechskant, Spudger, Kreuzschlitz (zum Ausbau der Platine)
schritte: 2. Begin by using a spudger to gently pry the top panel off. Be gentle as it is very thin plastic at high risk of bending or breaking.
4. Flip over the router and remove the bottom/wall mount piece.
5. Remove the two obvious hex screws. Note that one may have the sticker over it saying "Void Warranty"
6. There are two more hex screws buried in the side body.
7. ... top panel and bottom stand/mount are removed as well as six hex screws.
8. With a little force, pulling downward, away from the main body, remove the bottom.

9. ... while firmly depressing the power switch ..., pull the main body plastic upward towards the top. Be very careful ... the power toggle is very fragile and mine snapped off. The device still turns on but if you break it, the only way to force reboot is to cut power to it.
10. The body is now apart and the UART is now apparent. For further disassembly, use a cross head screwdriver.

openwrt_git_support.betreff: mediatek: filogic: add support ASUS RT-AX59U
openwrt_git_support.autor: Xavier Franquet (based on support for ASUS RT-AX59U by liushiyou006)
openwrt_git_support.text:
mediatek: filogic: add support ASUS RT-AX59U

(based on support for ASUS RT-AX59U by liushiyou006)

SOC: MediaTek MT7986
RAM: 512MB DDR4
FLASH: 128MB SPI-NAND (Winbond W25N01GV)
WIFI: Mediatek MT7986 DBDC 802.11ax 2.4/5 GHz
ETH: MediaTek MT7531 Switch
UART: 3V3 115200 8N1 (Pinout silkscreened / Do not connect VCC)

Upgrade from AsusWRT to OpenWRT using UART

    Download the OpenWrt initramfs image.
    Copy the image to a TFTP server reachable at 192.168.1.70/24. Rename the image to rtax59u.bin.

    Connect the PC with TFTP server to the RT-AX59U.
    Set a static ip on the ethernet interface of your PC.
    (ip address: 192.168.1.70, subnet mask:255.255.255.0)
    Conect to the serial console, interrupt the autoboot process by pressing '4' when prompted.

    Download & Boot the OpenWrt initramfs image.

    $ setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.1
    $ setenv serverip 192.168.1.70
    $ tftpboot 0x46000000 rtax59u.bin
    $ bootm 0x46000000

    Wait for OpenWrt to boot. Transfer the sysupgrade image to the device using scp and install using sysupgrade.

    $ sysupgrade -n <path-to-sysupgrade.bin>

Upgrade from AsusWRT to OpenWRT using WebUI

    Download transit TRX file from https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A20QdjK7Udagu31FSszpWAk8-cGlCwsq

    Upgrade firmware from WebUI (192.168.50.1) using downloaded TRX file

    Wait for OpenWRT to boot (192.168.1.1).

    Upgrade system with sysupgrade image using luci or uploading it through scp and executing sysupgrade command

MAC Address for WLAN 5g is not following the same algorithm as in AsusWRT.
We have increased by one the WLAN 5g to avoid collisions with other networks from WLAN 2g
when bit 28 is already set.

              : Stock             : OpenWrt
  WLAN 2g (1) : C8:xx:xx:0D:xx:D4 : C8:xx:xx:0D:xx:D4
  WLAN 2g (2) :                   : CA:xx:xx:0D:xx:D4
  WLAN 2g (3) :                   : CE:xx:xx:0D:xx:D4
  WLAN 5g (1) : CA:xx:xx:1D:xx:D4 : CA:xx:xx:1D:xx:D5
  WLAN 5g (2) :                   : CE:xx:xx:1D:xx:D5
  WLAN 5g (3) :                   : C2:xx:xx:1D:xx:D5

  WLAN 2g (1) : 08:xx:xx:76:xx:BE : 08:xx:xx:76:xx:BE
  WLAN 2g (2) :                   : 0A:xx:xx:76:xx:BE
  WLAN 2g (3) :                   : 0E:xx:xx:76:xx:BE
  WLAN 5g (1) : 0A:xx:xx:76:xx:BE : 0A:xx:xx:76:xx:BF
  WLAN 5g (2) :                   : 0E:xx:xx:76:xx:BF
  WLAN 5g (3) :                   : 02:xx:xx:76:xx:BF

openwrt_git_ubi.betreff: mediatek: add OpenWrt UBI layout for ASUS RT-AX59U
openwrt_git_ubi.text:
mediatek: add OpenWrt UBI layout for ASUS RT-AX59U

This commit implements the OpenWrt UBI layout for the ASUS RT-AX59U. The
primary goal is get working Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization
(KASLR). Additionally, this layout frees up ~6MB of extra storage space
for package installation.

Preparation
------------
Make a backup (from OpenWrt for stock bootloader):
* Backup partitions:
   apk update && apk add nand-utils
   nanddump /dev/mtd0 | gzip -1 -c > /tmp/mtd0_u-boot.bin.gz
   nanddump /dev/mtd1 | gzip -1 -c > /tmp/mtd1_UBI_DEV.bin.gz

* Backup nvram, Factory and Factory2 volumes:
   cat /dev/ubi0_0 > /tmp/nvram.bin
   cat /dev/ubi0_1 > /tmp/Factory.bin
   cat /dev/ubi0_2 > /tmp/Factory2.bin

* Copy backup from the /tmp dir on your router to a safe place using scp

Installation
------------
* Attach UART (see 'UART' section for details)

* Run mtkuartboot (see 'mtkuartboot recovery' section for details), exit
  the boot menu, and run:
   mtd erase ubi

* Run mtkuartboot again and write ubi bl2 and fip via the network, then
  reboot.

  Default tftp server ip: 192.168.1.254
  Default router ip:      192.168.1.1

* Load the ubi initramfs image via tftpboot and execute sysupgrade to
  write OpenWrt to spi-nand.

* Copy Factory backup to your router:
   scp -O Factory.bin root@192.168.1.1:/tmp

* Check factory volume index:
   ubinfo -a

* Prepare and write new factory ubi volume (substitute X with your
  factory volume index):
   dd if=/tmp/Factory.bin of=/tmp/factory.bin bs=1 count=$((0x65000))
   ubiupdatevol /dev/ubi0_X /tmp/factory.bin

UART
----
UART pins are silkscreened on PCB. Connection parameters:
115200, 8N1, 3.3V

U-Boot tftp recovery
--------------------
* Place OpenWrt ubi-initramfs-recovery.itb image on the tftp server (IP:
  192.168.1.254)

* Press reset button and power on the router. After ~10 sec release the
  button.

* Use OpenWrt initramfs system for recovery (for example, run sysupgrade)

mtkuartboot recovery
--------------------
Use mtk_uartboot and UART connetion for the installation or if BL2 or FIP
in UBI is destroyed:

Link: https://github.com/981213/mtk_uartboot

Start script:
'''
sudo ./mtk_uartboot \
  -p mt7986-ram-ddr4-bl2.bin \
  --aarch64 \
  -f openwrt-mediatek-filogic-asus_rt-ax59u-ubi-preloader.bin \
  -s /dev/ttyUSB0
picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0
'''

Notes
-----
1. A simple installation without serial console is also possible using a
   fork of Daniel's UBI Installer (requires adaptation)
Link: https://github.com/dangowrt/owrt-ubi-installer

Signed-off-by: Mikhail Zhilkin <csharper2005@gmail.com>
Link: https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/25278
Signed-off-by: Robert Marko <robimarko@gmail.com>

openwrt_git_spinand.betreff: mediatek: increase SPI-NAND frequency for ASUS RT-AX59U
openwrt_git_spinand.text:
mediatek: increase SPI-NAND frequency for ASUS RT-AX59U

Increase the spi-max-frequency from 20MHz to 52MHz for the SPI-NAND flash
on the ASUS RT-AX59U. The underlying Winbond W25N01KV chip natively
supports up to 104MHz, and the MediaTek MT7986A SoC safely handles 52MHz.

It's also 52 MHz in the stock U-Boot:
...
spi-max-frequency = <0x3197500>;
...

Testing with 'dd' reading 16MB from /dev/mtd1 shows a significant
performance improvement (~48% reduction in read time):

Before (20MHz):
256+0 records in
256+0 records out
real    0m 2.86s

After (52MHz):
256+0 records in
256+0 records out
real    0m 1.50s

Signed-off-by: Mikhail Zhilkin <csharper2005@gmail.com>
Link: https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/25278
Signed-off-by: Robert Marko <robimarko@gmail.com>

openwrt_git_ubidev.text:
mediatek: fix UBI_DEV partition size for ASUS RT-AX59U

Correct the UBI_DEV partition size from 252MB (0xfc00000) to 124MB
(0x7c00000). The previous value exceeded the physical limits of the
device, which features a 128MB flash chip.

openwrt_git_precal.text:
mediatek: add wireless pre-calibration data for ASUS RT-AX59U

Define the factory pre-calibration data partition at offset 0x1010 and
pass it to the wifi node via nvmem-cells. This ensures the mt7986
wireless hardware can properly utilize factory-calibrated RF settings.

openwrt_image_mk.asus_rt-ax59u:
define Device/asus_rt-ax59u-common
  DEVICE_VENDOR := ASUS
  DEVICE_MODEL := RT-AX59U
  DEVICE_DTS_DIR := ../dts
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := kmod-usb3 kmod-mt7915e kmod-mt7986-firmware mt7986-wo-firmware
endef

define Device/asus_rt-ax59u
  DEVICE_DTS := mt7986a-asus-rt-ax59u
  $(call Device/asus_rt-ax59u-common)
  IMAGE/sysupgrade.bin := sysupgrade-tar | append-metadata
endef
TARGET_DEVICES += asus_rt-ax59u

define Device/asus_rt-ax59u-ubi
  DEVICE_VARIANT := (UBI)
  DEVICE_DTS := mt7986a-asus-rt-ax59u-ubi
  $(call Device/asus_rt-ax59u-common)
  UBINIZE_OPTS := -E 5
  BLOCKSIZE := 128k
  PAGESIZE := 2048
  KERNEL_IN_UBI := 1
  UBOOTENV_IN_UBI := 1
  IMAGES := sysupgrade.itb
  KERNEL_INITRAMFS_SUFFIX := -recovery.itb
  KERNEL := kernel-bin | lzma
  KERNEL_INITRAMFS := kernel-bin | lzma | \
	fit lzma $$(KDIR)/image-$$(firstword $$(DEVICE_DTS)).dtb with-initrd | \
	pad-to 64k
  IMAGE/sysupgrade.itb := append-kernel | \
	fit lzma $$(KDIR)/image-$$(firstword $$(DEVICE_DTS)).dtb external-with-rootfs | \
	append-metadata
  ARTIFACTS := bl31-uboot.fip preloader.bin
  ARTIFACT/bl31-uboot.fip := mt7986-bl31-uboot asus_rt-ax59u
  ARTIFACT/preloader.bin := mt7986-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-1m-ddr4
endef
TARGET_DEVICES += asus_rt-ax59u-ubi

lauf.notiz: Kein Eintrag im ToH-Dump; Daten aus Live-hwdata (Rev. 2026-08-21) und OpenWrt-Wiki (Rev. 2026-10-10, inkl. Pinout- und Produktfoto), Support-Commit 782eb050 und Folge-Commits (Bootloader-Work-around, UBI-Layout/NAND-Frequenz/Pre-Cal 2026-09), DTS/DTSI und filogic.mk, Gluon upstream (nicht enthalten) und Neanderfunk-Patch 8dbae18 (werkstatt, ohne Messung), OpenWrt-Forum 154666 (134 Beitraege), WikiDevi-Spiegel, DeviWiki (keine Seite), ASUS-Techspec, ASUS-Handbuch E27382 v3 und EU-QSG, ASUS-Datenblatt 2022-12 (via Geizhals-CDN), Geizhals-Archivkopie 2023 (Permalink, ASIN). FCC-ID MSQ-RTAX5S00 aus ToH/WikiDevi gehoert zum TUF-AX4200 - als zweifelhaft markiert. Seriell: 4 unbestueckte Loetaugen VCC/GND/TX/RX innen, 3.3 V, 115200 8N1 (Forum spricht von Stiften). NAND-Varianten W25N01GV/W25N01KV/ESMT, U-Boot 2022.04-rc1 vs >=2022.10. Offen: EAN, Typenschild/H/W-Ver., echte FCC-ID, DC-Buchsenmass, Leistungsaufnahme, Luefter.
